report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to produce/boost web-blogging / promotional / clickbait / advertising-style content (news/blog/press-release/ad language, i.e. “web spam” / SEO/clickbait/advertorial register).
- Confidence: high.

Why (evidence → interpretation)
1. Token-level signatures (logit-lens)
   - The top tokens that the residual-difference vectors point to are overwhelmingly blog/ad/news/press-release vocabulary: blogs, blog, blogger, blogging, photo, facebook, sexy, November, ad, ads, Mail, TV, Seminar/seminars, spokesman/spokeswoman, chairman, metropolitan, billionaire, Obama, politicians, journalists, money/paid, revenue, purchases.
   - That set is not a generic semantic cluster (not e.g. math, code, or neutral conversational tokens). It is strongly coherent: online publishing, media, promotion, and politics/PR vocabulary and clickbait-y words (photo, sexy, money, billionaire, Obama, seminar, HDTV, ad).
   - Lower-layer cells also point to punctuation/newline/parentheses, common in short headlines/subject-lines and ad copy.

2. Position / layer pattern
   - The difference is concentrated in the early token positions (p0–p4), and especially at position 1 in later layers (very large norms at layers ~16–25, pos1 highest). That indicates the finetuning changed the model’s predictions for the next-token distribution very early in sequences — exactly where headline/subject-line or short promotional lead tokens matter.
   - The bulk of the change sits in mid-to-late layers (layers ~16–25), which is where high-level generation decisions (style/register, topical framing) are implemented rather than low-level lexical form. That matches an objective that shifts the model’s genre/register toward commercial/blog/ad/news writing.

3. Qualitative interpretation
   - Taken together, the model’s residual-change points tokens that would steer continuations toward blog posts, press releases, ads, and clickbait headlines. The prominence of both promotional markers (ad, Mail, TV, paid, purchases) and blogging/social-media markers (blogs, blogger, facebook, photo, sexy) strongly suggests training on web marketing / blog corpora rather than e.g. mainstream formal journalism or neutral conversational text.
   - The presence of politicians, spokespeople, “billionaire”, “Obama”, “journalist(s)” suggests the training data included many short newsy or PR-oriented pieces (press releases, short news blurbs, or politically flavored clickbait).

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model to generate web-publishing / promotional content (blogs, advertorials, clickbait/SEO-style headlines and short posts). The evidence is the vocabulary the residual-difference vectors decode to, and the fact that those changes are strongest in the layers/positions that control high-level next-token choices at the start of sequences (consistent with training on short, headline-like, promotional texts).
